summary: Over the 14-day period, the data shows excellent CGM coverage and a high Time in Range of 86.0%. However, there is a prominent safety risk with 5.1% Time Below Range, primarily concentrated in severe late-evening and overnight hypoglycemia (between 23:00 and 03:00). The system relies entirely on Unannounced Meals (UAM) and Dynamic ISF with extraordinarily wide safety limits, which drives aggressive insulin stacking that outpaces delayed food absorption.
issues: Severe and recurring nocturnal hypoglycemia between 23:00 and 03:00, reaching up to 18.5% Time Below Range at 01:00.
Maximum IOB (25 U) and Maximum Basal (12 U/h) limits in AAPS are set dangerously high, allowing the system to deliver excessive insulin unchecked.
The 90 mg/dL target from 23:00 to 08:00 provides almost no safety buffer against UAM-driven insulin stacking.
Total absence of logged carbohydrates forces the system to rely entirely on reactive UAM, which struggles with the delayed gastric emptying typically caused by GLP-1 therapy.
strengths: Exceptional CGM data coverage at 98.7% without missing data gaps.
Strong overall Time in Range (86.0%) despite the nocturnal lows.
System automation (SMB, UAM, Dynamic ISF) is highly active and responsive to glucose trends.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
The combination of GLP-1 therapy and unrestricted Max IOB limits (25 U) poses a severe risk of delayed hypoglycemia.
Discuss heavily reducing the maximum safety limits with the care team immediately to prevent dangerous insulin stacking.

analysis_steps.evidence: 14 days of data, 98.7% coverage, 3995 entries, 655 insulin entries. Zero carb entries logged.
analysis_steps.findings: CGM and insulin telemetry are highly reliable. However, the complete absence of logged carbohydrates means the system is operating in a 100% unannounced meal environment.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero carbohydrate inputs restrict the ability to evaluate Carb Ratios (CR) or meal absorption patterns.

analysis_steps.evidence: Time Below Range is 5.1%. Hourly TBR spikes to 11.4% at 00:00, 18.5% at 01:00, and 10.1% at 02:00. Event notes show active GLP-1 therapy.
analysis_steps.findings: There is a severe and recurring risk of late-evening and nocturnal hypoglycemia. The system repeatedly over-delivers insulin leading into the night.

analysis_steps.evidence: Targets are set at 90 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00. Basal rates hover around 0.5 to 0.8 U/h.
analysis_steps.findings: The 90 mg/dL nighttime target is too aggressive and offers no buffer for lingering active insulin. The system crashes through this tight target resulting in the observed 01:00 hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Difficult to decouple true basal needs from lingering unannounced meal insulin.

analysis_steps.evidence: ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U. DIA is 10 hours. CR segments exist but are unused.
analysis_steps.findings: A flat ISF of 56 combined with SMB/UAM may be too strong for the nighttime period, but cannot be safely evaluated until automation safety limits and targets are corrected.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: CR accuracy cannot be determined due to missing carb entries.

analysis_steps.evidence: UAM is enabled. max_iob_units is 25 U, max_basal_u_per_hour is 12 U/h. Loop logs show heavy reliance on UAM Boost.
analysis_steps.findings: The safety limits are extraordinarily wide for a profile with a max basal of 0.8 U/h. A 12 U/h max basal and 25 U max IOB give UAM practically unlimited freedom to stack insulin during a post-meal rise.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact meal timing must be inferred from CGM rises.

analysis_steps.evidence: Dynamic ISF is enabled with a 70% adjustment factor. Autosens is disabled.
analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF actively pushes the 56 ISF to much stronger values (e.g., 36 mg/dL/U) during spikes. Paired with the massive 25 U Max IOB limit, this creates a dangerous slingshot effect where massive doses are delivered, inevitably causing a crash.

analysis_steps.evidence: 0 carb entries in 14 days. 100% of boluses are driven by automation and unannounced meal detection.
analysis_steps.findings: The user relies exclusively on UAM. Because GLP-1 slows digestion, UAM misreads the initial glucose rise as a steep sustained spike, front-loads insulin, and causes severe lows when digestion tapers off.

analysis_steps.evidence: No e-carbs or extended boluses are utilized.
analysis_steps.findings: The lack of announced carbs means the system cannot model extended absorption, forcing it to react aggressively to the CGM delta rather than a known food profile.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Missing carb duration and composition data.

analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesis of severe night lows, 90 mg/dL target, 25 U max IOB, 12 U/h max basal, GLP-1 use, and 100% UAM strategy.
analysis_steps.findings: The primary threat is the combination of extreme safety limits and a tight overnight target while relying on UAM. Shrinking the max IOB and max basal limits, while simultaneously raising the nighttime target, will prevent the system from stacking lethal amounts of insulin and crashing the blood sugar.

recommendations.title: Constrain Safety Limits
recommendations.description: The max_iob_units limit of 25 U and max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 U/h are excessively high for a profile with basal rates under 1.0 U/h. This allows UAM to stack massive amounts of insulin. Reduce these to safe physiological multiples.

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target
recommendations.description: The 90 mg/dL target at 23:00 leaves no room for error when lingering UAM insulin from evening meals remains active. Raising this creates a much-needed safety buffer.

recommendations.title: Log Carbohydrates
recommendations.description: Relying 100% on UAM while on GLP-1 therapy causes insulin timing mismatches. Logging carbs, even without bolusing, will feed the algorithm absorption data to pace insulin delivery better.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The tight 90 mg/dL overnight target provides zero buffer against evening UAM insulin stacks, directly resulting in severe hypoglycemia between 23:00 and 03:00.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor if raising the target to 110 mg/dL eliminates the 00:00-03:00 hypoglycemia clusters.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise the 23:00 and 00:00 target segments to 110 mg/dL.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The system relies entirely on Unannounced Meals (UAM) without any logged carbohydrates, pushing AAPS to respond purely reactively to glucose trends.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Consider logging carbohydrate timing and amounts (even without manually bolusing) to give the system absorption data. This allows AAPS to pace insulin delivery more effectively alongside GLP-1 delayed digestion.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe whether logging carbohydrates smooths out the massive evening UAM insulin spikes and reduces subsequent nocturnal hypoglycemia.

implementation_steps: Discuss reducing max_iob_units to 5 U and max_basal_u_per_hour to 3 U/h to immediately mitigate the risk of severe insulin stacking.
Simultaneously raise the 23:00 and 00:00 targets to 110 mg/dL to provide a safety buffer against evening insulin tails.
Observe overnight glucose stability for 3-4 days after constraining safety limits and targets.
Begin logging carbohydrate events (time and amount) to provide the algorithm with absorption tracking, reducing the need for aggressive UAM responses.
education: GLP-1 medications slow gastric emptying, meaning glucose from food enters the blood more gradually over a longer period.

When you rely 100% on UAM, the algorithm looks at a quick rise and assumes an immediate need for lots of insulin. If digestion is delayed by a GLP-1, this front-loaded insulin outpaces the food absorption, causing low blood sugars hours later.

The max_iob_units limit is a crucial safety boundary. Setting it to 25 U when your basal is less than 1 U/h essentially removes the safety net, allowing the system to deliver massive correction boluses.
